title: Personal Data Protection Law: Purpose, Scope, and Definitions
summary: This page presents the header information and first chapter of Turkey's Personal Data Protection Law (No. 6698), accepted on 24/3/2016 and published in the Official Gazette on 7/4/2016 (No. 29677, Düstur 5th series, 57th volume). It covers the First Chapter titled 'Purpose, Scope and Definitions.' Article 1 (Purpose) states the law aims to protect individuals' fundamental rights and freedoms, particularly privacy, in the processing of personal data, and to regulate the obligations and procedures of natural and legal persons processing such data. Article 2 (Scope) specifies that the law applies to natural persons whose personal data is processed, as well as to natural and legal persons who process such data, whether fully or partially automatically or non-automatically, provided the non-automatic processing is part of a data recording system.

title: Tanımlar
summary: Article 3 of the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law provides definitions for key terms used throughout the legislation. It defines: explicit consent (informed, freely given consent on a specific matter); anonymization (making personal data irreversibly unidentifiable); Chairman (of the Personal Data Protection Authority); data subject (the natural person whose data is processed); personal data (any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person); processing of personal data (any operation performed on data, whether automatic or non-automatic, including collection, storage, modification, disclosure, transfer, and blocking); Board (Personal Data Protection Board); Authority (Personal Data Protection Authority); data processor (a natural or legal entity processing data on behalf of the data controller); data recording system (a structured system for processing personal data); and data controller (the entity determining purposes and means of processing and responsible for the data recording system).

title: İKİNCİ BÖLÜM

nodes.title: General Principles for Processing Personal Data – Article 4
nodes.summary: The text presents the Second Chapter on Processing of Personal Data, specifically Article 4 (General Principles). It establishes that personal data may only be processed in accordance with the procedures and principles set forth in this Law and other legislation. It then enumerates five mandatory principles that must be observed: (a) compliance with law and rules of good faith; (b) accuracy and, where necessary, currency of the data; (c) processing solely for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes; (d) relevance, limitation, and proportionality to the purposes for which the data are processed; and (e) retention for no longer than the period prescribed by relevant legislation or required for the processing purpose.

nodes.title: Kişisel verilerin işlenme şartları
nodes.summary: The text covers Turkish legal provisions (Articles 5-9) on personal data protection. Article 5 establishes that personal data processing requires explicit consent, listing seven exceptions (legal mandate, life protection, contract necessity, legal obligation, public disclosure, rights protection, legitimate interest). Article 6 defines special category data (race, religion, health, sexual life, criminal records, biometric/genetic data), prohibits processing without consent, allows exceptions for health/sexual data in public health contexts, and mandates adequate protective measures. Article 7 requires deletion, destruction, or anonymization of data when processing reasons cease, with procedures set by regulation. Article 8 governs domestic data transfer, permitting it without consent under Article 5(2) or 6(3) conditions. Article 9 regulates cross-border transfers, requiring adequate protection in the destination country or written commitments plus Board approval, with adequate-protection countries designated by the Board.

nodes.title: Kişisel verilerin aktarılması
nodes.summary: The text covers provisions on processing, deletion, and transfer of personal data under Turkish data protection law. It states that non-health/sexual personal data may be processed without explicit consent in legally foreseen cases, while health and sexual life data may only be processed without consent by confidentiality-bound persons/institutions for public health, preventive medicine, diagnosis, treatment, care, and health service planning/financing. Processing of special-nature data requires sufficient measures set by the Board. Article 7 mandates that personal data must be deleted, destroyed, or anonymized by the data controller when processing reasons cease, either automatically or upon request, with procedures regulated by regulation. Article 8 prohibits transferring personal data without explicit consent, except when conditions under Article 5(2) or Article 6(3) (with sufficient measures) are met. Provisions in other laws regarding deletion and transfer are preserved.

nodes.title: Kişisel verilerin yurt dışına aktarılması
nodes.summary: This text is Article 9 of Turkey's Personal Data Protection Law, governing the transfer of personal data abroad. It establishes that personal data cannot be transferred overseas without the data subject's explicit consent, except when conditions under Articles 5(2) or 6(3) are met and either adequate protection exists in the destination country or both data controllers provide written commitments to adequate protection with Board approval. The Board determines and announces countries with adequate protection. When evaluating adequacy and granting permissions, the Board considers international treaties, reciprocity, data nature/purpose/duration, destination country legislation, and committed safeguards, potentially consulting relevant institutions. Additionally, transfers may occur without consent in cases where Turkey's or the data subject's interests would be seriously harmed, subject to Board permission after consulting the relevant public institution. Finally, provisions in other laws regarding cross-border data transfers remain applicable.

nodes.title: ÜÇÜNCÜ BÖLÜM Haklar ve Yükümlülükler
nodes.summary: This text is from Chapter 3 (Rights and Obligations), specifically Article 10, which outlines the data controller's obligation to inform. It states that during the collection of personal data, the authorized person must inform the data subject about: (a) the identity of the data controller and their representative (if any), (b) the purpose for which personal data will be processed, (c) to whom and for what purpose the data may be transferred, (ç) the method and legal basis of data collection, and (d) the other rights enumerated in Article 11.

nodes.title: İlgili kişinin hakları
nodes.summary: The text covers two articles of a Turkish data protection law. Article 11 outlines the rights of data subjects, including: learning whether personal data is processed; requesting information about processed data; learning the processing purpose and whether data is used appropriately; knowing third parties (domestic or foreign) receiving the data; requesting correction of incomplete or inaccurate data; requesting deletion or erasure under Article 7 conditions; requesting notification of corrections/deletions to third parties; objecting to automated analysis producing adverse results; and claiming compensation for damages from unlawful processing. Article 12 details data security obligations of data controllers: taking technical and administrative measures to prevent unlawful processing, access, and ensure data preservation; joint responsibility when data is processed by another entity; conducting or commissioning audits; prohibition on disclosing or using data beyond its purpose (even after leaving the position); and the obligation to promptly notify the data subject and the Board in case of unauthorized access, with the Board potentially publishing the incident.

summary: This section covers Turkey's Personal Data Protection Law, spanning Chapter 2 (Processing of Personal Data) and the start of Chapter 3 (Rights and Obligations). It establishes five general principles for data processing: legality, accuracy, purpose limitation, proportionality, and retention limits. It defines processing conditions requiring explicit consent with seven exceptions, and sets special rules for sensitive data (health, biometric, criminal records). It mandates deletion, destruction, or anonymization when processing reasons cease. It regulates domestic and cross-border transfers, requiring adequate protection or Board-approved safeguards. It outlines the data controller's obligation to inform data subjects about identity, purpose, transfers, and collection method. It enumerates data subject rights including access, correction, deletion, objection to automated analysis, and compensation claims. Finally, it details data security obligations: technical/administrative measures, joint responsibility, audits, and breach notification to the data subject and the Board.

title: DÖRDÜNCÜ BÖLÜM
summary: This text is Chapter 4 of Turkey's Personal Data Protection Law, covering: (1) Article 13 – Data subjects' right to apply to data controllers in writing, with a 30-day response deadline, fee provisions, and acceptance/rejection procedures including refunds for controller errors. (2) Article 14 – Complaints to the Board when applications are rejected, insufficiently answered, or unanswered, with 30/60-day time limits, mandatory exhaustion of the application route, and preserved compensation rights. (3) Article 15 – Board's investigation procedures upon complaint or ex officio, document submission obligations (15 days), 60-day response deadline, violation remediation orders (30-day compliance), principle decisions for widespread violations, and authority to suspend data processing or cross-border transfers. (4) Article 16 – The public Data Controllers' Registry, mandatory pre-processing registration with possible exceptions, required registration details (identity, purpose, data categories, recipients, foreign transfers, security measures, retention period), obligation to report changes, and regulatory provisions.

nodes.title: Kabahatler
nodes.summary: The text covers Article 18 (administrative fines for violations of notification, data security, Board decisions, and registry obligations, ranging from 5,000 to 1,000,000 TL, applicable to natural persons and private entities, with disciplinary actions for public institutions), Article 19 (establishment of the Personal Data Protection Authority with administrative/financial autonomy, public legal personality, headquartered in Ankara, composed of a Board and Presidency, linked to a President-appointed minister), Article 20 (Authority's tasks including tracking developments, research, cooperation with institutions and international bodies, and submitting annual reports), and Article 21 (the Board's independence, composition of 9 members—5 elected by TBMM and 4 by the President—and membership requirements including expertise, civil servant qualifications, non-party membership, and a bachelor's degree). Footnotes note amendments made by KHK 703/163 in 2018.

nodes.title: (4) (Mülga: 2/7/2018-KHK-703/163 md.)
nodes.summary: The text covers the selection, duties, and powers of board members of a data protection authority. It details: (1) TBMM's proportional selection process based on party group quotas, voting procedures, timelines, and replacement elections; (2) presidential selection and replacement timelines; (3) the board electing its President and Vice President; (4) a four-year renewable term with oath before the Court of Cassation; (5) restrictions on members (no other employment, trade, or arbitration) with exceptions for academic activities; (6) criminal investigation procedures under Law 4483 and disciplinary proceedings under Law 657; (7) grounds for termination of membership; (8) post-term employment and payment arrangements; and (9) the board's duties and powers (Article 22), including ensuring lawful personal data processing, handling complaints, conducting inspections, determining security obligations, maintaining the Data Controllers Registry, issuing regulatory acts, imposing administrative sanctions, providing opinions on legislation, approving strategic plans, budgets, performance reports, and real estate decisions.

nodes.title: Kurulun çalışma esasları
nodes.summary: The text outlines Article 23 on the Council's working principles. It covers: (1) the President's authority to set meeting schedules, agendas, and call extraordinary meetings; (2) quorum requirements (minimum six members including the President) and decision-making by simple majority with no abstentions permitted; (3) recusal rules requiring members to abstain from matters involving themselves, close blood relatives (up to 3rd degree), in-laws (up to 2nd degree), adopted children, or spouses; (4) confidentiality obligations prohibiting disclosure or personal use of learned secrets, persisting after leaving office; (5) documentation requirements for minutes, decisions, and dissenting opinions within 15 days, with optional public announcements; (6) default confidentiality of Council discussions; and (7) delegation of detailed procedures to a regulation.

nodes.title: Başkan
nodes.summary: The text covers Articles 24-27 of a Turkish data protection authority law. Article 24 defines the President's role as the institution's top authority, detailing duties such as managing board meetings, appointing staff, preparing strategic plans and budgets, ensuring coordination, and representing the institution externally; the Second President serves as deputy. Article 25 describes the Presidency's structure (Deputy President and up to seven directorates), qualification requirements (4-year degree, 10 years public service), and extensive duties including maintaining the Data Controllers Registry, legal representation, HR management, IT systems, financial services, procurement, and strategic planning. Article 26 allows employment of Personal Data Protection Specialists with a one-time degree increase. Article 27 addresses personnel rights: subject to Law 657, equivalent financial/social rights to comparable public servants, social insurance under Law 5510, pension calculations, temporary assignment of public servants (capped at 10% of specialist positions, max 2 years extendable), and cadre management by board decision.

nodes.title: İstisnalar
nodes.summary: Article 28 of Turkey's Personal Data Protection Law outlines exceptions where the law's provisions do not apply. Paragraph 1 lists full exemptions: (a) personal/household data processing by natural persons; (b) processing for official statistics, research, and planning (anonymized); (c) processing for art, history, literature, science, or freedom of expression, provided no violation of national security, public order, privacy, or criminal law; (ç) processing by public institutions for preventive, protective, and intelligence activities; (d) processing by judicial or enforcement authorities for investigation, prosecution, trial, or execution. Paragraph 2 lists partial exemptions (Articles 10, 11 except damages claim, and 16 do not apply) for: (a) crime prevention/investigation; (b) data made public by the data subject; (c) public institution supervision, regulation, or disciplinary proceedings; (ç) protection of state economic and financial interests. A 2017 amendment added judges' and prosecutors' consent requirement.

nodes.title: Kurumun bütçesi ve gelirleri
nodes.summary: The text covers an institution's budget and revenue provisions, amended/added legal references, regulations, and transitional provisions. Article 29 states the budget follows Law 5018 and lists revenue sources: treasury aid, property income, donations, revenue evaluation income, and other income. Article 30 references amendments incorporated into Laws 5018, 5237, 3359, and 663. Article 31 assigns the institution authority to issue implementing regulations. Transitional provisions (Temporary Article 1) mandate: board member selection and presidency formation within 6 months; data controller registration within a set period; compliance of pre-existing personal data within 2 years (with deletion/anonymization of non-compliant data and 1-year validity of prior consents); regulation issuance within 1 year; designation of a senior coordination manager in public institutions within 1 year; staggered terms (6 years for President, Vice President, and 2 members; 4 years for 5 others); and interim funding and secretariat services provided by the Prime Ministry until the institution's budget is allocated and service units become operational.

nodes.title: GEÇİCİ MADDE 2- (Ek:28/11/2017-7061/120 md.)
nodes.summary: This temporary article (added 28/11/2017, Law 7061/120) defines eligibility for appointment as a Personal Data Protection Expert. Candidates must hold a minimum four-year degree in political sciences, economics, law, business, or specific engineering fields (electronics, electrical, communications, computer, information systems) from YÖK-recognized domestic or foreign institutions. They must have been appointed via a special competitive exam, completed in-service training and a proficiency exam, and served at least two years (excluding unpaid leave) in central organization positions under Law 657, Article 36(A)(11), or hold a teaching faculty position. Additional requirements include scoring at least 70 on the Foreign Language Proficiency Exam and not having turned 40 at the time of appointment. Appointments must occur within one year of the article's effective date, with a maximum of 15 such positions.

nodes.title: Yürütme
nodes.summary: The text covers three main sections: (1) Article 33, the execution clause stating that the Council of Ministers shall implement the Law's provisions. (2) Schedule I, the personnel/staffing list of the Personal Data Protection Authority, detailing 195 positions across various classes (GİH, AH, TH, YH) and grades, including roles such as Deputy Chairman, Department Head, Legal Advisors, Lawyers, Personal Data Protection Experts and Assistants, Financial Services Experts, Clerks, Computer Operators, Data Preparation and Control Operators, Secretaries, Switchboard Operators, Drivers, Technicians, and Service Staff. (3) A table listing the effective dates of amendments to Law No. 6698 made by subsequent legislation or annulled by the Constitutional Court: Law No. 7061 (Articles 27 and Provisional Article 2, effective 5/12/2017) and Decree-Law No. 703 (Articles 19, 20, 21, 25, effective 9/7/2018, the date the President took office after the 24/6/2018 elections).

The section covers criminal and administrative penalties for personal data violations (referencing Turkish Penal Code Articles 135-140 and fines of 5,000–1,000,000 TL). It establishes the Personal Data Protection Authority, detailing its structure, Board composition (9 members selected by TBMM and the President), selection procedures, working principles (quorum, voting, recusal, confidentiality), and the President's role. It outlines the Authority's tasks, personnel structure and rights, specialist appointment eligibility requirements, budget and revenue sources, full and partial exceptions to the law, transitional provisions with compliance timelines, staggered entry-into-force dates, execution by the Council of Ministers, a 195-position staffing schedule, and the amendment history of the legislation.

summary: This section addresses criminal and administrative penalties for personal data violations under Turkish Penal Code Articles 135–140, including fines ranging from 5,000 to 1,000,000 TL. It establishes the Personal Data Protection Authority, detailing its organizational structure, nine-member Board composition selected by the TBMM and the President, selection procedures, and working principles such as quorum, voting, recusal, and confidentiality. The section outlines the Authority's tasks, personnel structure and rights, specialist appointment eligibility, budget and revenue sources, and the President's role. It further covers full and partial exceptions to the law, transitional provisions with compliance timelines, staggered entry-into-force dates, execution by the Council of Ministers, a 195-position staffing schedule, and the amendment history of the legislation.
